issue.title: fix(opd): reverse staff welfare and credit on multi-payment batch cancel (#25348)
issue.body:
## Summary
Fixes #25348.

When an OPD batch bill settled with `MultiplePaymentMethods` had only a single payment entry (for example, settled entirely via Staff Welfare or Staff Credit), `OpdBatchBillCancellationController.initializePaymentDataFromOriginalPayments` overrode the controller's `paymentMethod` to that single row's payment method.

Because batch bills do not store `toStaff` at the bill level for multi-payment transactions, the single-payment cancellation branches failed to update staff balances:
- `cancellationBatchBill.getToStaff()` evaluated to `null`.
- The multi-payment settlement branch `paymentService.updateBalances(cancelPayments)` was bypassed because `cancellationBatchBill.getPaymentMethod()` was no longer `MultiplePaymentMethods`.

Consequently, canceling such OPD batch bills did not credit back the staff member's welfare or credit balance.

## Changes
- **Payment Method Preservation**: In `initializePaymentDataFromOriginalPayments`, keep `paymentMethod` as `MultiplePaymentMethods` if `batchBill.getPaymentMethod()` is `MultiplePaymentMethods`, even when `originalPayments.size() == 1`.
- **Single-Method Staff Fallback**: In `initializePaymentDataFromOriginalPayments` for `Staff` and `Staff_Welfare`, initialize controller `toStaff` from `originalPayment.getToStaff()` if not already set.
- **Session State Isolation**: Reset `paymentMethodData` in `navigateToCancelOpdBatchBill()` and at the start of `initializePaymentDataFromOriginalPayments()` to prevent cross-bill state retention in `@SessionScoped` bean.
- **Strict Staff Fallbacks**: In `cancelOpdBatchBill` and `cancelPackageBatchBill`, apply staff fallbacks strictly to `PaymentMethod.Staff` and `PaymentMethod.Staff_Welfare`. Company `PaymentMethod.Credit` only updates staff credit if `toStaff` was explicitly present on the bill.
- **Package Multi-Payment Balance Updates & Payment Rows**:
  - In `cancelPackageBatchBill`, invoke `paymentService.updateBalances(cancelPayments)` when `cancellationBatchBill.getPaymentMethod() == PaymentMethod.MultiplePaymentMethods`.
  - In `createPaymentForOpdBatchBillCancellation()`, populate staff, amount, and comment on `Staff` and `Staff_Welfare` payment rows created during package cancellations.
- **Unit Tests**:
  - Added `OpdBatchBillCancellationStaffReversalTest` covering:
    - Multi-payment batch bills with a single payment row retain `MultiplePaymentMethods` and preserve staff associations on `ComponentDetail`.
    - Single-method `Staff_Welfare` bills populate `toStaff` from original payment rows when bill-level `toStaff` is null.
    - Single-method `Staff` credit bills populate `toStaff` from original payment rows when bill-level `toStaff` is null.
    - Single-method `Credit` bills reset `paymentMethodData` and do not inherit stale staff credit from prior session cancellations.

## How it was tested
- Ran `mvn test -Dtest=OpdBatchBillCancellationStaffReversalTest` (JDK 11): 4/4 tests passed (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
- Verified full test compilation with `mvn test-compile`.

## Checklist
- [x] Branched from `upstream/development`
- [x] Target branch is `development`
- [x] Follows repository coding style and architectural guidelines
- [x] Commit message includes DCO sign-off (`Signed-off-by`)

issue.title: PaymentService.updateStaffCredit updates welfare, so multi-payment staff credit is never reversed on cancel
issue.body:
## Problem
`PaymentService.updateStaffCredit(Payment)` (called from `updateBalances` for `Staff` payment rows) calls `staffService.updateStaffWelfare(...)`, so a staff-credit component of a Multiple Payment Methods bill moves the staff's **welfare utilised** figure instead of their **current credit**, and it looks up the staff only from `bill.toStaff` (null for multi-payment bills), so in practice it usually does nothing.

As a result, cancelling a multi-payment bill with a Staff (staff credit) component does not reverse the staff credit.

## Why it was not fixed in #20549
Switching it to `updateStaffCredit` changes every `updateBalances` caller. Several settle paths already credit the staff inline and then call `updateBalances` (review on #25338), e.g. `OpdOrderController` (~1939 then ~1954), `PharmacySaleController1/2/3` (~3190 then ~3194), and the inline multi-payment credit in `OpdBillController`, `OpdOrderController`, `BillPackageController`, `PharmacySaleController*`. The fix would double-apply credit there.

## Proposed approach
1. Audit every `paymentService.updateBalances(...)` caller and every inline `updateStaffCredit` in the same flow.
2. Make one place own the staff-credit update per flow (preferably `updateBalances`, using `payment.toStaff` then `bill.toStaff`), removing the inline calls, and make sure every Staff payment row stores `toStaff` (OPD multi-payment rows do since #25338).
3. E2E: settle and cancel with single Staff and with Cash + Staff, on OPD, OPD order, package and pharmacy sale; credit must rise once and return to the start value.

Related: #20549, #25338

comment.body:
### Call-Site Audit and Implementation Analysis for #25339

Following up on the proposed approach in the issue description, here is the audit of `paymentService.updateBalances(payments)` callers and inline `updateStaffCredit` calls:

#### 1. Core Defect in `PaymentService.java` (lines 744–753)
```java
private void updateStaffCredit(Payment p) {
    if (p == null || p.getBill() == null) {
        return;
    }
    if (p.getBill().getToStaff() == null) {
        return;
    }
    Staff toStaff = p.getBill().getToStaff();
    staffService.updateStaffWelfare(toStaff, p.getPaidValue()); // <-- Bug: calls updateStaffWelfare, ignores p.toStaff
}
```
In contrast, `updateStaffWelare` (lines 755–775) resolves `p.getToStaff()` first with fallback to `p.getBill().getToStaff()`, and updates the welfare ledger.

#### 2. Dual-Update Settle Call Sites (Call inline `updateStaffCredit` then `updateBalances`)
In the following settle flows, the controller manually invokes `staffBean.updateStaffCredit` and then calls `paymentService.updateBalances(payments)`:
- `OpdOrderController.java`: line 1939 (`staffBean.updateStaffCredit`), line 1954 (`updateBalances`).
- `PharmacySaleController.java`: line 3905 (`getStaffBean().updateStaffCredit`), line 3909 (`updateBalances`).
- `PharmacySaleController1.java`, `Controller2`, `Controller3`: line 3190 (`getStaffBean().updateStaffCredit`), line 3194 (`updateBalances`).
- `PharmacyFastRetailSaleController.java`: line 1793 (`getStaffBean().updateStaffCredit`), line 1827 (`updateBalances`).
- `PharmacySaleForCashierController.java` (and variants 1, 2, 3): line 4765 (`getStaffBean().updateStaffCredit`), line 4769 (`updateBalances`).
- `PharmacySimpleRetailSaleController.java`: line 361 (`getStaffBean().updateStaffCredit`), line 376 (`updateBalances`).
- `BillPackageController.java`: line 1914 (`staffBean.updateStaffCredit` on custom data in multi-payment).

#### 3. Cancellation Paths (Rely on `updateBalances` to reverse)
When a bill or batch bill is cancelled, cancellation controllers build negated `cancelPayments` and call `paymentService.updateBalances(cancelPayments)`:
- `BillController.java:2746`
- `OpdBatchBillCancellationController.java:2869`
- `OpdBillCancellationController.java:803`
- `BillReturnController.java:872`
- `InwardSearch.java:2242`

Because `PaymentService.updateStaffCredit` previously called `updateStaffWelfare` and did not resolve `p.getToStaff()`, cancellation never deducted from the staff's credit balance.

#### 4. Recommended Fix Architecture
1. **In `PaymentService.java`**:
   Update `updateStaffCredit` to check `p.getToStaff()` first, fallback to `p.getBill().getToStaff()`, and invoke `staffService.updateStaffCredit(toStaff, p.getPaidValue())`.
2. **Consolidate Settle Ownership**:
   Retire the redundant inline `staffBean.updateStaffCredit` calls in the controllers listed above where `updateBalances(payments)` immediately follows, establishing `updateBalances` as the single canonical owner of payment-method ledger updates across both single-payment and multi-payment workflows.

issue.title: feat(pharmacy): add item suppliers API for bulk price list linking (#25060)
issue.body:
### Summary
Fixes #25060 (Part of #25059).

Provides a dedicated REST API under \/api/pharmacy/item_suppliers\ to create, list, bulk link, and retire \ItemsDistributors\ links between pharmaceutical items (AMPs/AMPPs) and suppliers (Dealers). This replaces single-item linking in the GUI (\pharmacy/pharmacy_items_distributors.xhtml\) and provides validated linking with full audit attribution when loading supplier price lists.

### Changes
- **Data Transfer Objects (\com.divudi.core.data.dto.pharmacy\)**:
  - \ItemSupplierDto\: Link details including IDs, names, codes, orderNo, and creation/retire audit attribution.
  - \ItemSupplierRequestDto\: Single request payload (\supplierId\, \itemId\, \orderNo\).
  - \BulkItemSupplierResultDto\: Per-row batch response model (\supplierId\, \itemId\, \outcome\, \code\, \id\, \message\, \data\).
- **Service Layer (\PharmacyItemSupplierApiService\)**:
  - Validates supplier is an unretired Dealer institution (\InstitutionType.Dealer\); returns 400 otherwise.
  - Validates item is an unretired pharmaceutical item (\Amp\ or \Ampp\); returns 400 otherwise.
  - Detects existing active links and returns HTTP 409 Conflict with the existing row.
  - Implements bulk linking supporting array, object, or fan-out structures with individual row error isolation.
  - Filters out active links on retired items from search queries to match GUI behavior.
  - Soft-retires links with full audit logging attribution via \AuditService\.
- **REST Endpoints (\PharmacyItemSupplierApi\)**:
  - Authenticated using standard \Finance\ API key header.
  - \GET /api/pharmacy/item_suppliers?supplierId=&itemId=&limit=&offset=\: Search active links with pagination (excluding retired items).
  - \GET /api/pharmacy/item_suppliers/{id}\: Retrieve a single link by ID.
  - \POST /api/pharmacy/item_suppliers\: Create single link (201 Created / 409 Conflict / 400 Bad Request).
  - \POST /api/pharmacy/item_suppliers/bulk\: Bulk link with per-row outcomes and strict integer parsing for fan-out payloads.
  - \DELETE /api/pharmacy/item_suppliers/{id}?retireComments=\: Soft-retire link (200 OK / 404 Not Found).
- **Registration & Docs**:
  - Registered resource in \ApplicationConfig\ and \CapabilityStatementResource\.
  - Added documentation guide \developer_docs/api/using-apis/API_PHARMACY_ITEM_SUPPLIERS.md\ clarifying malformed JSON batch rejection vs row-level validation.
  - Updated \developer_docs/api/using-apis/README.md\.
- **Unit Tests**:
  - Added \PharmacyItemSupplierApiServiceTest\ (17 tests) covering creation, missing fields, 404s, 400s (non-dealer, non-Amp/Ampp, retired item/supplier), duplicate 409 conflict, mixed bulk outcomes, retirement audit fields, idempotency, and search filtering.
  - Added \PharmacyItemSupplierApiTest\ (6 tests) covering bulk payload parsing variations and strict rejection of fractional/malformed IDs.

### How It Was Tested
- Verified clean compilation with JDK 21.
- Executed full JUnit 5 test suite: 23/23 tests passed cleanly.

issue.title: fix(pharmacy): link or find-or-create VMPP in AMPP API (#25061)
issue.body:
## Problem
\POST /api/pharmaceutical_items/ampp\ creates an AMPP without an associated VMPP (\^Gmpp.vmpp\ remains null), unlike the GUI which invokes \PharmacyBean.getVmpp(ampp, packUnit)\. Additionally, updating an AMPP's pack size or pack unit leaves the VMPP association un-synchronized.

Fixes #25061 (supersedes #25063 per review request).

## Changes
- **VMPP link & auto-resolution:**
  - \AmppRequestDTO\: Added optional \mppId\ field with getters and setters.
  - \AmppDto\: Added \mppId\ and \mppName\ fields, constructor overload, \getVmppDisplay()\, and updated \	oString()\.
  - \createAmpp\: Runs \ indDuplicateByName\ check first. Validates explicit \mppId\ against the AMP's VMP, pack size, and pack unit. When omitted, automatically resolves or creates the matching VMPP if the AMP has a VMP, a positive \dblValue\, and a valid pack unit.
  - \updateAmpp\: Validates all target references and \mppId\ *before* mutating any fields on the managed entity. If pack dimensions change such that prerequisites are no longer met (e.g. \dblValue <= 0\ or missing unit), clears the stale VMPP association.
  - \ indOrCreateVmpp\: Uses \mppFacade.createAndFlush(v)\ so generated ID is available immediately for the response DTO, sets \DepartmentType.Pharmacy\, and propagates parent VMP category.
  - \alidateExplicitVmpp\: Rejects retired VMPPs, pack size / unit mismatches, orphan AMPs (no VMP), and VMP mismatches with HTTP 400.
  - \searchAmpps\: Updated JPQL projection to include \mpId\, \mpName\, \mppId\, and \mppName\.
- **Exception & Transaction Rollback:**
  - Introduced \PharmaceuticalItemApiException\ annotated with \@ApplicationException(rollback = true)\ so validation failures rollback the EJB transaction and map directly to HTTP 400 or 404 in \PharmaceuticalItemApi\.
- **Documentation:**
  - Updated \developer_docs/api/using-apis/API_PHARMACEUTICAL_MANAGEMENT.md\ with explicit \mppId\ validation and clearing semantics.
- **Unit Tests:**
  - Added \PharmaceuticalItemApiServiceTest\ (9 tests) and \PharmaceuticalItemApiExceptionTest\ (2 tests).

- **Known gap:** there is no unique constraint behind the VMPP lookup, so two concurrent requests for the same (VMP, pack size, unit) can create duplicate VMPPs. This matches `PharmacyBean.getVmpp` and is documented.

issue.title: fix(lib): stop mutating shared Intl options in parseDateTimeWithTimeZone
issue.body:
## Summary

Closes #30510

`parseDateTimeWithTimeZone` in `packages/lib/parse-dates.ts` maintained two **module-level** `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` objects (`timeOptions` / `dateOptions`) that were **directly mutated** on every call:

```ts
// Before (broken)
timeOptions.timeZone = timezone;      // leaks caller's timezone into next call
// ...
delete timeOptions.hour12;            // permanently removes the key from the singleton
```

This caused two related bugs:

| Call sequence | Symptom |
|---|---|
| 24 h call → 12 h call | 12 h call renders without am/pm because `hour12` was deleted by the prior call |
| call with TZ-A → call with TZ-B | second call renders in TZ-A until the assignment overwrites it on the same tick |

## Fix

Rename the singletons to `BASE_TIME_OPTIONS` / `BASE_DATE_OPTIONS` (naming signals read-only intent) and **shallow-clone** them into per-call locals via object spread before applying any per-invocation overrides:

```ts
// After (fixed)
const timeOptions = { ...BASE_TIME_OPTIONS, timeZone: timezone };
const dateOptions = { ...BASE_DATE_OPTIONS, timeZone: timezone };
```

Each invocation is now fully independent of its predecessor.

Also adds an explicit `hour12: true` restoration in the h12 branch so the property is always set, not just absent.

## Tests

Added `packages/lib/parse-dates.test.ts` (picked up by the existing vitest workspace config):

- `withDefaultTimeFormat` always forces h12 output
- `selectedTimeFormat: TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR` renders without am/pm
- **24 h → 12 h sequence produces am/pm** (core regression case)
- **24 h → omitted options defaults to 12 h am/pm** (added per CodeRabbit review in `c9c9fd1`)
- Consecutive 12 h calls remain stable
- Different timezones in back-to-back calls produce different output

## Checklist

- [x] Root cause fixed (not just the reproduction sample)
- [x] Tests added covering all call-sequence permutations
- [x] Kept PR small and focused (2 files, <100 LOC)
- [x] No changes to public API or types
- [x] DCO signed commits

issue.title: fix(bookings): format overlay busy times using booker slot timezone (#30418)
issue.body:
﻿## Summary
Closes #30418.

In `useCheckOverlapWithOverlay`, `start` is provided in the booker's selected timezone, but `busyDateStart` and `busyDateEnd` were parsed into the browser's local OS timezone (`dayjs(busyDate.start)`). Consequently, changing the timezone in the booker UI caused the overlap tooltip (`overlappingTimeStart` / `overlappingTimeEnd`) to display times in the local OS timezone instead of the selected booker timezone, and multi-day day boundary checks were evaluated against the wrong timezone.

### Changes
- Bound `busyDateStart` and `busyDateEnd` to the timezone offset of `start` (`.utcOffset(start.utcOffset())`).
- Added a regression test in `useCheckOverlapWithOverlay.test.ts` checking slot timezone offset formatting.

## Test plan
- Added unit test: `formats overlapping times using the timezone offset of the start slot` in `packages/features/bookings/lib/useCheckOverlapWithOverlay.test.ts`.
- Confirmed that a 10:00 UTC busy date checked against a +05:00 slot correctly formats as `15:00 - 16:00`.

issue.title: [Bug]: locking acquire() with several keys keeps the keys it got when one is busy, so acquireLockStep can't retry and the keys block others until TTL
issue.body:
### Package.json file

```json
"@medusajs/medusa": "2.21.2",
"@medusajs/framework": "2.21.2",
"@medusajs/core-flows": "2.21.2",
"@medusajs/locking": "2.21.2",
"@medusajs/locking-redis": "2.21.2"
```

### Node.js version

v24.12.0

### Database and its version

PostgreSQL 18.6, Redis 7

### Operating system name and version

macOS (Darwin 25.6); also reproduced on Ubuntu 24.04 in CI

### Browser name

n/a (backend only)

### What happended?

Acquiring several keys at once (`locking.acquire(["a", "b"])`, or `acquireLockStep({ key: [...] })`) is not all-or-nothing. When one key is held by someone else, the call throws, **but keeps the keys it already took**.

Without an `ownerId`, those leftover keys can't be taken again, not even by the same caller:
- In-memory, they're stored with `ownerId: null`. The "same owner" branch requires `lock.ownerId !== null`.
- In Redis, they're stored as `"*"`. The Lua script returns 0 for `"*"`.

So `acquireLockStep`'s retry loop (`timeout`) can never succeed after a partial failure. Every other caller is also blocked on the leftover keys until the TTL expires.

We hit it in a checkout workflow that locks `[cart:<id>, stock:<variant>:<location>, ...]`. Two overlapping carts at once: one fails on a shared stock key, keeps its cart key, retries until timeout, and the stock keys it did get block other checkouts for the full TTL.

**Cause:**
- `InMemoryLockingProvider.acquire_` (`packages/modules/locking/src/providers/in-memory.ts`) loops over the keys and sets each free one, then throws on the first busy one without undoing the earlier sets.
- `RedisLockingProvider.acquire_` (`packages/modules/providers/locking-redis/src/services/redis-lock.ts`) runs one `acquireLock` per key in parallel (`promiseAll`). The successful ones stay set when another rejects.
- `acquireLockStep` (`packages/core/core-flows/src/locking/steps/acquire-lock.ts`) retries the same ownerless `acquire` until `timeout`, so the retry always fails on its own leftover keys.

### Expected behavior

A failed multi-key `acquire` leaves no keys held, or at least lets the same caller retry. Then `acquireLockStep({ key: ["a", "b"], timeout })` succeeds once `b` is released.

### Actual behavior

After `acquire(["a", "b"])` fails on `b`:
- `a` stays locked, with owner `null` in memory or `*` in Redis, until its TTL.
- Retrying after `b` is released fails on `a`.
- Any other caller is blocked on `a`.

### Link to reproduction repo

No public repo. Minimal repros against the installed providers:

```js
// In-memory
const { InMemoryLockingProvider } = require("@medusajs/locking/dist/providers/in-memory")
const p = new InMemoryLockingProvider()
await p.acquire("b")                       // someone else holds b
await p.acquire(["a", "b"]).catch(e => e)   // Failed to acquire lock for key "b"
p.locks.has("a")                           // true, ownerId null
await p.release("b")
await p.acquire(["a", "b"])                // throws: Failed to acquire lock for key "a"
```

```js
// Redis
const { RedisLockingProvider } = require("@medusajs/locking-redis/dist/services/redis-lock")
const p = new RedisLockingProvider({ redisClient: new Redis(url), prefix: "repro_lock:" }, {})
await p.acquire("b", { ownerId: "other", expire: 30 })
await p.acquire(["a", "b"], { expire: 30 }).catch(e => e) // Failed to acquire lock for key "b"
await redis.get("repro_lock:a")                            // "*", TTL 30
await p.release("b", { ownerId: "other" })
await p.acquire(["a", "b"], { expire: 30 })                // throws: Failed to acquire lock for key "a"
```

**Workaround** (what we do now): use our own step that passes an `ownerId` unique to the workflow run (`transactionId`), calls `release(keys, { ownerId })` after a failed attempt before retrying, and releases with the same `ownerId`.

**Suggested fix:**
- Make multi-key `acquire` atomic, or release the keys taken in the failed call before throwing.
- And/or have `acquireLockStep` default `ownerId` to the transaction id.

### What happended?

When a BuyGet (BUYGET) promotion is applied to line items that already have discounts from previously applied promotions, the BuyGet promotion can calculate its discount using the original item amount instead of the remaining eligible amount.

In `packages/modules/promotion/src/utils/compute-actions/buy-get.ts`, the methods `getComputedActionsForBuyGet` and `applyPromotionToTargetItems` appear to retrieve the previously applied promotion value through `methodIdPromoValueMap.get(item.id)`, but this value is not properly accounted for when calculating the applicable discount amount.

For example:

- Line item quantity: 3
- Unit price: 199
- Original subtotal: 597
- Previously applied discount: 500
- Remaining eligible amount: 97

When a subsequent BuyGet promotion applies a 100% discount to one unit, the discount is calculated as 199 instead of being limited to the remaining eligible amount of 97.

This results in:
- Total discounts: 699
- Final line item total: -102

Similarly, when a fixed discount of 150 is applied after the previous discount of 500, the combined discounts total 650, resulting in a negative line item total of -53.

This behavior appears to occur because the BuyGet discount calculation does not adequately account for previously applied promotion adjustments when determining the remaining eligible amount.

### Expected behavior

BuyGet promotions should account for previously applied promotion adjustments when calculating the remaining eligible amount of a line item.

The discount applied by a subsequent promotion should be capped at the remaining eligible item value and should never cause the line item's total to become negative.

If the line item has already been fully discounted, the subsequent BuyGet promotion should not apply any additional discount to it.

The promotion calculation should consistently respect accumulated promotion values, similar to the handling in other promotion computation paths such as line items and shipping methods.

### Actual behavior

BuyGet promotions calculate discounts without properly subtracting previously applied promotion values from the eligible amount.

This allows subsequent discounts to exceed the remaining value of the line item.

For the example above:
- Original subtotal: 597
- Previous discount: 500
- Remaining eligible amount: 97
- Subsequent BuyGet discount: 199
- Final line item total: -102

The line item ends up with a negative total, even though the total discounts should not exceed the original subtotal.

issue.title: [Bug]: buyget promotions apply the discount to items with is_discountable: false
issue.body:
### Package.json file
Reproduced inside the medusajs/medusa monorepo on develop at 396aa3f510 (@medusajs/promotion 2.21.2). The relevant code is unchanged in the published 2.21.x packages. No custom package.json involved; the repro below runs against the promotion module's own integration test runner.

### Node.js version
v22.22.2

### Database and its version
PostgreSQL 17.5

### Operating system name and version
macOS 15.7.3

### Browser name
Not applicable

### What happended?
A product can be marked as not discountable (product.discountable = false, surfaced on cart items as is_discountable: false). Standard promotions respect that flag: the item filter in the promotion module's compute-actions code skips any line with is_discountable: false, so a 100% standard promotion targeting a gift card produces no adjustment.

Buyget promotions do not. getComputedActionsForBuyGet in packages/modules/promotion/src/utils/compute-actions/buy-get.ts builds its eligible target items with filterItemsByPromotionRules, which only evaluates the target rules and never looks at is_discountable. So a "buy 1 shirt, get 1 gift card at 100%" promotion discounts the gift card to zero even though the merchant marked gift cards as not discountable.

I checked the 8,000-line compute-actions.spec.ts for this module: there is no test with is_discountable: false at all, so nothing guards either path.

### Expected behavior
A buyget promotion never produces an adjustment on an item with is_discountable: false, the same way standard promotions behave. Non-discountable items should still be allowed to satisfy the buy rules (buying a gift card can qualify you for a discounted shirt), they just should not receive the discount.

### Actual behavior
computeActions returns an addItemAdjustment for the non-discountable item:

Context: shirt (is_discountable: true, category catg_shirt, subtotal 1000) and gift card (is_discountable: false, category catg_gift, subtotal 500).

Standard promotion, 100% percentage, target rule items.product_category.id eq catg_gift:
  computeActions(["STD"], context) -> []

Buyget promotion, buy_rules items.product_category.id eq catg_shirt, target_rules items.product_category.id eq catg_gift, 100%, apply_to_quantity 1, buy_rules_min_quantity 1:
  computeActions(["BG"], context) -> [{ action: "addItemAdjustment", item_id: "item_gift_card", amount: 500, code: "BG" }]

### Link to reproduction repo
No separate repo needed, it reproduces directly against PromotionModuleService with the module's own moduleIntegrationTestRunner (packages/modules/promotion/integration-tests):

```ts
const context = {
  currency_code: "usd",
  items: [
    { id: "item_shirt", quantity: 1, subtotal: 1000, original_total: 1000, is_discountable: true,
      product_category: { id: "catg_shirt" }, product: { id: "prod_shirt" } },
    { id: "item_gift_card", quantity: 1, subtotal: 500, original_total: 500, is_discountable: false,
      product_category: { id: "catg_gift" }, product: { id: "prod_gift" } },
  ],
}

await service.createPromotions({
  code: "BG",
  type: "buyget",
  application_method: {
    type: "percentage", target_type: "items", value: 100, allocation: "each",
    max_quantity: 1, apply_to_quantity: 1, buy_rules_min_quantity: 1,
    buy_rules: [{ attribute: "items.product_category.id", operator: "eq", values: ["catg_shirt"] }],
    target_rules: [{ attribute: "items.product_category.id", operator: "eq", values: ["catg_gift"] }],
  },
})

const result = await service.computeActions(["BG"], context)
// expected: []
// actual:   [{ action: "addItemAdjustment", item_id: "item_gift_card", amount: 500, code: "BG" }]
```

Swap type to "standard" with the same target rule and the result is [], which is the behaviour I would expect from buyget too.

## Problem
`ChannelReportController.fillNurseView()` lists bill types `ChannelAgent`, `ChannelCash`, `ChannelOnCall` and `ChannelStaff` only. It leaves out `ChannelCredit`, which the sibling queries in `BookingControllerViewScope` include.

A rescheduled credit booking gets a `ChannelCredit` reschedule bill, and plain credit bookings are `ChannelCredit` too.

On the Nurse View pages filled by `fillNurseView()` (`channel/channel_views/channel_nurse_view.xhtml`, `channel_nurse_view_with_items.xhtml`, and the older `channel/channel_nurse_view.xhtml`), credit bookings are missing from the list. A rescheduled credit booking shows as "Rescheduled" in its old session but does not appear at all in its new session.

## Fix
Add `BillType.ChannelCredit` to the bill-type list in `fillNurseView()`, after checking what the session page's Nurse View tab (`bookingControllerViewScope.billSessions`) includes, so all Nurse Views list the same bookings.

Found while reviewing #24799.

## Problem
On the session page (`channel/session_instance.xhtml`), the **Nurse View With Items** tab's **Download** (Excel) writes `com.sun.faces.facelets.component.UIRepeat@...` in the **Items** and **Value** columns instead of the item names and values. issue.title: Credit company dropdowns show Institution[ id=... ] instead of names (var="cc" collides with JSF implicit object)
issue.body:
## Symptom
Credit company dropdowns and autocompletes on several report pages show `lk.gov.health.entity.Institution[ id=... ]` (dropdowns) or blank suggestions (autocompletes) instead of the company name.

Seen live on **Inpatient Analytics → Payment Reports → All Deposit of Not Discharged Patient**: every option in the credit company dropdown reads `lk.gov.health.entity.Institution[ id=... ]`.

## Cause
These pages use `var="cc"` as the loop variable in `f:selectItems` / `p:autoComplete`, with `itemLabel="#{cc.name}"`. `cc` is the reserved JSF implicit object for the enclosing composite component, so the EL resolver resolves `#{cc}` to that object, not to the loop variable. The label falls back to `Institution.toString()` (or is blank).

#22666 found and fixed the same cause on one page only. The remaining occurrences:

```
src/main/webapp/analytics/email_list.xhtml
src/main/webapp/credit/inward_bht_credit_payment_report.xhtml

src/main/webapp/inward/inward_charge.xhtml

src/main/webapp/inward/inward_report_professional_done_payment.xhtml
src/main/webapp/inward/inward_report_professional_payment_due.xhtml

src/main/webapp/inward/report_income_room.xhtml
```

`developer_docs/ui/comprehensive-ui-guidelines.md` (the `p:autoComplete` "CORRECT" example near line 556) also shows `var="cc"`, so new code copies the bug. It was copied into #24472 and caught during testing there.

## Steps
1. Log in, select a department, open Inpatient Analytics → Payment Reports → All Deposit of Not Discharged Patient.
2. Open the credit company dropdown.

**Expected:** credit company names. **Actual:** `lk.gov.health.entity.Institution[ id=... ]`.

## Fix direction
- Rename the loop variable on every listed page (e.g. `var="crCo"`, used consistently in `itemLabel` / `itemValue`).
- Fix the example in the UI guidelines and add a one-line rule: never use `cc` as an EL `var` name.

## Impact
Display only: the selected value is still the right institution, so filtering works. Users must guess which entry is which company, though, which makes these reports hard to use when there are many credit companies.

issue.title: Admission: 'admitted successfully' shown alongside the cancellation error when automatic charges fail
issue.body:
## Symptom
When automatic admission charges fail during *Inpatient → Admissions → Patient Admit*, the admission is correctly cancelled, but the user sees two contradictory messages at once:

- "Patient admitted successfully with BHT No: …"
- "Automatic admission charges could not be applied and this admission has been cancelled. Please retry."

A user reading the first message may believe the patient is admitted.

## Cause
`AdmissionController.saveSelected()` adds the success message right after `getFacade().create(getCurrent())` (`src/main/java/com/divudi/bean/inward/AdmissionController.java:3183`), and only later calls `applyAutomaticAdmissionCharges(...)` (`:3328`), which can retire the admission. `saveConvertSelected()` has the same order (`:3380` then `:3419`).

## Steps
1. Configure an automatic admission charge for an admission type.
2. Admit a patient of that type while the charge run fails (e.g. a DB error while the charge bills are saved).
3. Both growls appear.

## Expected
Only the error message. The success message should be added after the automatic charges have succeeded.

## Fix direction
Move the "admitted successfully" message to after `applyAutomaticAdmissionCharges(...)` returns `true` in both save paths (or clear the faces messages before adding the error).

## Impact
Low. It needs a charge-run failure, and the error message is shown too, but the two messages contradict each other. Found while verifying #24573.

comment.body: Hi Dr. @buddhika75, I would like to work on this issue. In AdmissionController.java, the success message is added immediately upon getFacade().create(getCurrent()) at line 3216 and 3413, before applyAutomaticAdmissionCharges(...) is evaluated. If the charges fail, both error and success messages appear. I will move the success message to execute only after applyAutomaticAdmissionCharges(...) returns true in both saveSelected() and saveConvertSelected(). Could you please assign this to me?

issue.title: patient_details composite shows stale shared-phone search list on read-only Inward pages
issue.body:
## Symptom
**Edit BHT**, **Manage Allergies** and the **Inpatient Pharmacy Item List** report show a "Name / Phone Number / select" list instead of the admitted patient's details. This happens after the user has run a phone quick-search elsewhere in the same session that matched two or more patients and selected none.

## Cause
`src/main/webapp/resources/ezcomp/common/patient_details.xhtml` has the same render conditions that #24417 fixed in `patient_details_for_addmission.xhtml` (lines 32, 105, 133, 360). They read the session-scoped `patientController.quickSearchPatientList` and ignore the component's `searchable` attribute. These pages use the composite with `searchable="false"`:
- `inward/inward_edit_bht.xhtml:220`
- `inward/inward_manage_allergies.xhtml:46`
- `inward/reports/inpatient_pharmacy_item_list.xhtml:61`

Line 360 (`quickSearchPatientList eq null`) also hides the details view. The list's **select** button would swap the controller's patient for a different person.

## Steps
1. Inpatient → Admissions → Patient Admit → quick-search a phone number shared by two patients and select neither.
2. Open Edit BHT (or Manage Allergies) for any admission through the menus.

## Expected
The admission's patient is shown.

## Fix direction
Apply the same change as PR #24538: the list only takes effect when `cc.attrs.searchable`, and the view, header and edit panels use `not cc.attrs.searchable or empty patientController.quickSearchPatientList`.

## Impact
Found by reading code while fixing #24417, not reproduced live on these pages. The trigger is the same as #24417, which was reproduced.

issue.title: Blank/whitespace reason bypasses required-comment checks (session leave, collecting-centre payment cancel)
issue.body:
## Symptom
Two "reason/comment is required" checks can be bypassed by leaving the box blank or typing only spaces.

## Cause
JSF submits a blank `p:inputText` as `""`, not `null` (`web.xml` does not set `INTERPRET_EMPTY_STRING_SUBMITTED_VALUES_AS_NULL`). These guards therefore don't catch it:

- `src/main/java/com/divudi/bean/channel/ServiceSessionLeaveController.java:105` and `:118`: `getDeactivateComment() == null` only. A blank "reason for leave" passes.
- `src/main/java/com/divudi/bean/common/CollectingCentrePaymentController.java:1010`: `comment == null || comment.isEmpty()`. A spaces-only comment passes.

## Steps (leave)
1. Channelling → add a doctor leave for a service session (by session or by date).
2. Leave the reason box empty and save.

**Expected:** "Please Enter a Reson For Leave". **Actual:** the leave is saved with an empty reason.

## Fix direction
Use `x == null || x.trim().isEmpty()` in each guard. This is the same fix as #24517 (BHT issue / transfer request cancellation).

## Impact
Low. Audit text is missing; no financial or stock effect. Found by code reading while fixing #24517.

comment.body: Hi Dr. @buddhika75, I would like to take this up. I verified that ServiceSessionLeaveController.java (getDeactivateComment() == null) and CollectingCentrePaymentController.java (comment == null || comment.isEmpty()) allow blank/whitespace reasons to pass because JSF submits empty inputs as empty strings. I will update both guards to use trim().isEmpty() following the pattern in #24517 and add unit tests. Please assign this to me.

issue.title: Date of Birth field placeholder shows wrong format (dd/mm/yyyy) vs actual accepted pattern (dd/MMM/yyyy)
issue.body:
## Summary
Several shared Date of Birth `p:datePicker` fields show a placeholder hint that does not match the pattern the field actually accepts, so typing the hinted format produces a "could not be understood as a date and time" error.

## Where
Found while testing #24564 on the Patient Admission page, but the same composite/placeholder text is duplicated across at least 5 files:
- `src/main/webapp/resources/ezcomp/common/patient_details_for_addmission.xhtml:213`
- `src/main/webapp/resources/ezcomp/common/patient_details.xhtml:223`
- `src/main/webapp/resources/ezcomp/common/patient_details_for_appoiment.xhtml:209`
- `src/main/webapp/resources/ezcomp/cc_self_billing_patient_details.xhtml:231`
- `src/main/webapp/inward/inward_appointment_edit.xhtml:276`

Each has:
```xml
pattern="dd/MMM/yyyy - hh:mm:ss a"
...
placeholder="Date of Birth (dd/mm/yyyy - hh:mm:ss a)"
```
The `pattern` (what the field actually parses) uses `MMM` (3-letter month name, e.g. `Jan`), but the `placeholder` tells the user `mm` (numeric month), so typing e.g. `01/01/1990 00:00:00` is rejected with `'01/01/1990 00:00:00' could not be understood as a date and time. Example: 18/Oct/2026 - 06:21:28`.

## Expected
Placeholder text should match the actual `pattern`, e.g. `Date of Birth (dd/MMM/yyyy - hh:mm:ss a)`.

## Impact
Low — the date picker widget itself still works when used via the calendar UI; this only misleads someone typing the date directly.

comment.body: Hi Dr. @buddhika75, I would like to work on this issue. I have identified the 5 composite and page files where placeholder='Date of Birth (dd/mm/yyyy - hh:mm:ss a)' conflicts with pattern='dd/MMM/yyyy - hh:mm:ss a'. I will update the placeholder text to dd/MMM/yyyy to match the parser pattern and verify against the test suite. Could you please assign this to me?
